children: is in advanced talks to sell its remaining stake in its central and eastern Europe operations to private equity firm CVC Capital Partners
in a deal that could value the division at between £1.5 billion and £1.75 billion ($1.96 billion to $2.29 billion), Sky News reported on Saturday, citing sources.
Entain holds a 47.5% stake in the CEE business, having offloaded a 20% interest to joint venture partner EMMA Capital in June for €425 million ($466.1 million)
Entain said at the time it would keep evaluating options to fully exit the business, which owns SuperSport in Croatia and STS in Poland
According to Sky, there are other interested parties

Entain is under pressure to cut costs to offset increases in Britain's gambling taxes. It expects an extra £25 million hit to its UK and Ireland retail business after the government raised taxes on the industry for a second consecutive year in last month's budget
Entain declined to comment on the report, while CVC did not immediately respond to a request for comment sent outside regular business hours
